title: Independent source noise left 54 to 58 percent covariance error in eight worm site models with fixed gains
abstract: We tested whether independent whole-source fluctuations can reproduce shared-site noise covariance in eight selected C. elegans anatomical maps. A fixed panel had 149 neuron-like labels. With known positive unit gains and equal independent site variance, projection onto all real source variance coefficients left 53.9 to 57.6 percent relative off-diagonal covariance error. Nonnegative fits left 54.4 to 58.1 percent. Fractional gains and removal of the largest source kept nonzero errors. A residual-based linear contrast removes all independent source variance under these assumptions. Direct sums, separate projection calculations and two synthetic cases passed. These are model differences, not measured brain noise. Correlated sources, uncertain gains, recurrent dynamics, partial anatomy and unknown release laws limit biological use. Code, aggregate results, exact input hashes and retrieval steps support reproduction. External records and matrices remain outside the baseline bundle.

display.caption: Relative distance from shared-site covariance to the linear span of independent source covariance patterns, under three fixed feedforward gain and selection rules. These are conditional model results, not measured neural noise.
